AI video editor in Claude Code: 3 prompts, from an empty folder to a finished reel. SETUP (once) 1. Get the Claude app (claude.ai/download) and open the Code tab, not the browser. 2. Make a folder "AI Editor" with 3 folders inside: raw, references, done. 3. New chat in Code → Local → Select folder → AI Editor. Needs a paid Claude plan. PROMPT 1: TOOLS You're my video editor. We work in this folder: raw, references, done. Install and verify 5 tools: FFmpeg with libass (on Mac: ffmpeg-full, full path), faster-whisper for word-level subtitles, yt-dlp for references, Remotion, HyperFrames (npm package hyperframes). Check what's installed first. Official installs only (Homebrew, winget, npm/pip), Node.js 22+. Python packages go in a .venv here, Python 3.14 or older: pip install faster-whisper "av<19". Test each for real: burn a subtitle into a test clip, transcribe 5 seconds of audio. Show a table: tool, version, works or not. PROMPT 2: YOUR TASTE Here are reels whose editing I like: [link 1] [link 2] [link 3]. My format: [talking to camera / voiceover]. Download them with yt-dlp into references (for study only). Study each one frame by frame and by ear: pacing, shot length, pause cuts, subtitles, colors, graphics, transitions, music, the first 3 seconds. Take inspiration, but don't copy: no shots, text, logos or brand elements. Write my own style to style.md with exact values. Show it and ask what to change. PROMPT 3: EDIT My new recording is in raw. Edit it using style.md: 1. Transcribe with Whisper, word timestamps. Ask me about doubtful words before burning subtitles. 2. Cut pauses, slips and bad takes, keep the last good take. Check cut points by audio level. Keep pauses that serve the meaning, breaths and word endings. Don't speed up my voice. 3. Word-by-word subtitles in my style. 4. If references/music.mp3 exists, put it quietly under the voice. 5. Graphics only where they help. 6. Export 1080×1920 to done as draft-v1.mp4 plus edit-notes.md. Check the file yourself, then show me. I'll give edits in plain words; save each as draft-v2, draft-v3. No code words. Follow for my own editing style, coming next.

Building an app with AI? Learn these 4 parts first Want to build an app with AI? Learn the four parts first: the front end, the back end, the database, and where AI fits in a modern app. When you ask ChatGPT or Claude to build you an app (vibe coding, no code), these four parts are what you're actually describing. Explained for complete beginners. We follow one customer message through an online coffee store app, start to finish: 1. Front end: everything the customer sees and taps. The screens, the buttons, the text box. It doesn't know prices or stock. It shows things and passes messages along. 2. Back end: runs on a server the customer never sees. This is where the business rules live: login, stock, prices, payments. The front end asks, the back end decides. 3. Database: where everything is saved, like a giant spreadsheet that never closes. Products, prices, customers, orders. Only the back end opens it, and it checks who's asking. 4. AI in the middle: the back end calls the AI model only for jobs that need understanding. Job one, turn a plain sentence ("a gift for my dad, he drinks it black, under $40") into a search. Job two, write the answer using only the real products the database sent back. The rule for building reliable AI apps: AI handles the words, the back end handles the facts and the money. Never let the AI make up prices or stock. Whole app in four lines: the front end shows, the back end decides, the database remembers, the AI understands and writes. If you want to go from understanding the four parts to building your own apps with AI, I teach it step by step, from complete beginner to real systems. OpenJarvis - a free, open source personal AI assistant you run on your own computer. Made by Stanford researchers (Hazy Research + Scaling Intelligence Lab), not me. #openjarvis #claudecode #aiagents #opensource #ai Repo: github.com/open-jarvis/OpenJarvis Install, Mac / Linux - paste the repo link into Claude Code and say "install this for me", or run it yourself: curl -fsSL open-jarvis.github.io/OpenJarvis/install.sh | bash (add the https prefix to the address) Windows: the install.ps1 command from the README, or the desktop app from Releases. Morning briefing in 3 commands: jarvis init --preset morning-digest-mac --force   (or -linux / -minimal) jarvis connect gdrive   (one Google sign-in covers Gmail, Calendar, Tasks) jarvis digest --fresh   (or just say "good morning" in the chat) If jarvis isn't found, put uv run in front of it. Heads up: - The spoken briefing uses a Cartesia or OpenAI API key (paid). Free: jarvis digest --text-only to read it (a local open source Kokoro voice is also in the code). - Gmail needs your own Google OAuth client (client_id:client_secret), the docs walk you through it. - Models run locally through Ollama, so your computer has to handle a local model. Cloud models are optional. - The installer asks about anonymous analytics - answer N if you don't want it. - The 40 emails in the video are an example, not a test result. No code words - everything's right here. Follow arti.miller - next I'll play you the first real briefing my Jarvis gives me.

AI can now generate cinematic videos up to 5 minutes long that look like they were filmed by an actual production crew. @openart_ai has an AI tool called Director Mode and you can create the entire cinematic video just by telling it what you want. It handles the scenes, camera movement, voices, and music all in one place. Here’s how it works: I uploaded a few photos of a property and said: “Turn these property photos into a cinematic walkthrough with a voiceover and music. Start outside, show the main rooms, and then finish with the view.” Check out the result. It turned those photos into a full property video with smooth camera movement. The craziest part is it puts the whole video together without you having to stitch in the clips yourself. It plans out how the scenes flow so you get an opening, a buildup, and a final reveal. You can also ask it to make changes like “slow down the living room shot, make the music softer, and spend more time showing the view.”  Director Mode updates the video based on that feedback while keeping the visuals and voice consistent across every scene. #OpenArtPartner #AI #AITools #AIVideo
